answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires each identity to solve a unique computational puzzle before participating. The puzzle seed incorporates a public echo of the previous epoch's valid answers, forcing fresh work. An attacker cannot reuse solutions across identities; each fake agent demands dedicated CPU time on its own knoll of hardware. Scaling to thousands of identities multiplies the hardware and energy cost linearly, while honest agents pay only once. This keeps the meadow of active participants costly to flood with duplicates.
